title: Non-negative Integers without Consecutive Ones
summary: For a positive integer n, calculate the count of integers within the range [0, n] that have binary representations without consecutive ones.
statement: For a positive integer n, calculate the count of integers within the range [0, n] that have binary representations without consecutive ones.
constraints: Count every integer in the inclusive range 0 through n whose binary representation contains no adjacent 1 bits.
hints: The valid binary strings of each length follow a Fibonacci recurrence.
Scan n from high bit to low bit, counting valid smaller prefixes whenever n has a 1.
Precompute counts[k]=counts[k-1]+counts[k-2]; add counts[bit] for each set bit and stop on 11.
At a set bit, choosing zero yields every valid shorter suffix. Choosing one continues only if the preceding prefix did not already end in one, which gives the Fibonacci count and the early stop.
editorial: Let counts[k] be the number of length-k bit suffixes with no consecutive ones, including leading zeros. The two possible starting bits yield counts[k]=counts[k-1]+counts[k-2]. While reading n, every set bit permits a smaller prefix by selecting zero and then any valid suffix. A second consecutive set bit means the exact prefix is invalid, so no larger suffix can repair it. If the scan completes, n itself is valid and is included. The independent oracle enumerates small seeded values directly; the same reference is never used as its oracle.

tests.explanation: 0, 1, 2, 4, and 5 have no consecutive ones, for five values.
Both 0 and 1 are valid in the inclusive range.
